Meeting header:

Summary (auto): short qualification, show Console JSON mode, demo of schema enforcement and typed outputs, runtime fallbacks demo (model variant + region fallback), discuss VPC/private, SOC2/KMS, agree pilot next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Liam Ortega from Redwood, AE. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Aisha: Good, thanks. Quick note, we have Dana from security and Marcello — we might jump around to technical details.
[00:15] Priya: Awesome. We'll kick with a two minute context check then jump into the console and a runtime demo. If anything, interrupt.
[00:22] Marcello: Sounds good. Quick qualification: we are running mostly on AWS EKS, some internal embeddings service, and we've got a small in-house agent prototype. Latency targets are 200-300ms p95 for user-facing flows. Cost matters — we're optimizing for cost per convo.
[00:38] Liam: Great, that's exactly what we want to validate today. One clarifying q — is data residency a hard constraint?
[00:44] Dana: Yes, EU data must stay within our EU account. We're also evaluating bringing Redwood Private into our VPC, or at least a dedicated tenancy.
[00:53] Priya: Ok. We'll show hosted patterns and the private/VPC options later. For the demo, we'll focus on JSON mode — schema-first outputs and safe tool invokes — and then show how the runtime falls back to a smaller quantized model when capacity is constrained.
[01:10] Tom: Quick FYI, our infra team cares about KMS integration and audit logs — those are blockers for pilot sign-off.
[01:16] Liam: Noted. We have KMS + HSM integrations and token-level audit tracing; we'll share the security snapshot after.
[01:22] Priya: Alright I'm going to screenshare the Console. (slight pause) Can you all see the Console?
[01:31] Aisha: Yes. Font is small but yup.
[01:35] Priya: Cool. Top-left is the JSON Mode tab — here we define a schema as a contract. I'll paste a quick schema for an agent 'action' that returns typed steps. You can see we validate at runtime and provide a sandboxed function registry.
[01:50] Priya: (typing) Ok schema: action_name (string), params (object), confidence (number). When the model returns, we enforce the contract and can auto-cast or fail safely to a fallback.
[02:05] Marcello: Is that enforcement at the API proxy or inside the runtime?
[02:09] Priya: Inside the runtime layer — the inference engine will attempt to coerce weak matches, but if it's a hard schema failure we surface a controlled error and can route to a fallback plan. That avoids weird downstream failures.
[02:22] Unknown (Contractor): Does that add latency?
[02:24] Priya: Minimal — schema check is microseconds relative to token generation. The bigger impacts are batch size and KV cache lookups, which we also show in the Console's per-route latency breakdown.
[02:36] Liam: I'll pull up a short notebook showing the API call pattern. (shares link) Here we call /v1/generate with response.mode=json and a schema id.
[02:48] Aisha: If the schema doesn't match, can we trigger a retry with stricter decoding or a different sampling?
[02:54] Priya: Yes — we have an automatic 'strictify then retry' policy. You can also set a fallback to a deterministic sampler or a smaller cost-optimized model variant.
[03:04] Dana: Walk me through the safe tool calling story. We're worried about arbitrary web calls or data exfil.
[03:11] Priya: Absolutely. The Console's tool registry is sandboxed. Tools are whitelisted per-model and per-route. We support parameter validation on tool inputs, output schema enforcement, and a dry-run mode in the Console. For network calls, we can force them through a private egress in your VPC or sandbox with allowed domains only.
[03:30] Marcello: Can we see an example of a function call — like call a search API and then call an enterprise DB?
[03:35] Priya: Yep. I'll kick off a demo flow: user query -> model extracts an intent -> we call internal search (mocked) -> we call a structured DB write (simulated).
[03:45] [03:45] Priya: (executes) The model returns an action object: {action_name: "search_docs", params: {query: "postgres schema migration"}, confidence: 0.87}. Console shows syntax highlight and validation passed. It then executed the registered 'search_docs' tool in sandbox; I have that mapped to a mocked endpoint.
[03:58] Aisha: Good, I like seeing the validation. In your logs I noticed KV cache hits — how does prefill work for agent context?
[04:06] Priya: We expose prefix cache and per-session KV. You can pin context into the KV and the runtime will do an incremental KV cache lookup. It's visible in the tracing panel and you can see token savings and cost impact.
[04:18] Tom: For the agent flow, can we limit which tools a model can call per user role? We need RBAC.
[04:23] Priya: Yes, RBAC is supported at the route and tool level. Console maps roles to capabilities, and we log all tool invocations with requestor identity.
[04:32] Marcello: Walk me through fallback behaviors — what happens when the primary model is at capacity?
[04:36] Priya: We have policy-driven routing. Example: route to gptx-large in us-west-2, if capacity full, fallback to quantized gptx-small in same region, if region degraded, fallback to cross-region compatible variant. You can set cost- or latency-first policies. We also can degrade gracefully: return a partial structured response with a 'degraded' flag.
[04:58] Liam: I want to show a quick live fallback sim — switching to a smaller quantized model mid-request. (changes the runtime policy)
[05:08] [05:08] Priya: Triggered simulated contention. You can see the request was proxied and the response includes a fallback_reason: "capacity" and additive metadata.
[05:20] Dana: Will fallback trigger a new SLO or alert? We need to know when user-visible degradations happen.
[05:25] Priya: Yes — Console exposes per-route SLOs and fallback counts; you can create alerts when fallback_rate > threshold.
[05:33] Aisha: How would a pilot look operationally? We want to test agent workflows and a search rerank flow.
[05:39] Liam: Typical is a 4-week pilot: week 0 onboarding + network setup (VPC peering or private connector), week 1-2 run ingest and pilot traffic, week 3 evaluate cost/perf and run evals, week 4 ramp or freeze. We'll share a pilot SLA.
[05:54] Marcello: Are there any known issues with EKS integration? We've seen weird MTU problems in other tools.
[05:59] Priya: We integrate via private connector and peering; sometimes customers need an egress NAT tweak — we have a network runbook for common MTU/firewall issues. I'll attach that.
[06:10] Tom: On KMS: does Redwood support customer-managed keys across Dedicated and Private?
[06:15] Liam: Yes. Customer KMS support is available for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can integrate with your KMS for at-rest artifacts via customer-supplied keys in most regions. We'll include specifics in the security snapshot.
[06:27] Unknown (Contractor): Any performance numbers for quantized variants?
[06:30] Priya: Our bench sheet has throughput/latency numbers. Quantized small model runs ~2-3x cheaper for long sequences with p95 ~1.7x latency compared to fp16 large depending on token length and batching. I'll pull up a quick plot.
[06:45] [06:45] Priya: (shares bench) Here you can see sequence length vs tokens/sec. For your 200-300ms p95 target, we recommend a hybrid: keep front-end user queries on a low-latency small variant, and heavier reasoning on a larger model with asynchronous follow-up.
[07:05] Marcello: For the structured output, how do you handle hallucination where model returns invalid enum values?
[07:10] Priya: Two layers: 1) schema validation will reject or coerce; 2) we can run a lightweight verifier chain that re-checks outputs against a small retrieval set or deterministic rules before executing tools. If verifier fails, we don't call the tool — we surface the issue to the orchestrator.
[07:26] Dana: That verifier — is it an extra LLM call? Latency impact?
[07:29] Priya: It's pluggable — could be rule-based or LLM-based. For low-latency flows we use deterministic checks or param constraints. LLM-based verification can be async or run with a tiny model to keep latency low.
[07:43] Aisha: Can we lock models per-route so legal knows what was used for outputs?
[07:48] Liam: Yes — model pinning and versioned model references are supported. All requests log model_id and model_hash for auditability.
[07:56] Marcello: About rollout: can we do a canary where 5% of traffic uses a new model and 95% the old?
[08:01] Priya: Absolutely. Rollouts with traffic splits, A/B, automatic rollback on metric regression — all in Console. We'll show a quick canary config after lunch — I mean after the next section.
[08:12] Aisha: (laugh)
[08:15] Liam: Quick check — any non-starters so far?
[08:19] Dana: KMS specifics and SOC2 artifacts are mandatory. Also need proof of encryption in transit for the private path.
[08:27] Liam: We'll include TLS+ mutual TLS options.
[08:30] Priya: Next I'll demo a live run from the API — showing response.mode=json with a schema and a function call that writes an event to a simulated DB then returns a typed ack.
[08:41] [08:41] Priya: (runs API) Here's the raw response: {"action_name":"log_event","params":{"event_type":"user_feedback","score":4},"confidence":0.91}. Console schema shows validation passed and a trace entry with step-by-step.
[08:55] Marcello: The trace shows token counts — can we export per-request billing?
[08:59] Liam: Yes — we have token-level cost breakdowns exportable per API key. That helps with sandboxed dev keys.
[09:06] Tom: For pilot scale, what's the SLA delta between Hosted and Dedicated?
[09:10] Liam: Hosted offers standard best-effort with limits; Dedicated gives committed throughput and SLA-backed latency and uptime. We'll share a table in the pricing doc.
[09:20] Marcello: Any red flags from the demo?
[09:22] Dana: Mostly security paper details.
[09:24] Aisha: I think this shows what we need. The schema enforcement plus safe tool sandbox is attractive.
[09:30] Liam: Great. Quick recap and next steps: Priya will send GIF/notebook with JSON-mode quickstart, Liam will send pilot pricing and dedicated capacity options, Dana will share a short list of security questions and KMS requirements. We aim to confirm pilot scope by 2026-06-12.
[09:49] (crosstalk)
[09:49] Marcello: Thanks, this was helpful.
[09:51] Priya: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with notes and links.

End transcript.

Notes and artifacts shared in chat: Deck link, security snapshot PDF, benchmark spreadsheet.
